title: google-deepmind/formal-conjectures
abstract: Formal proof of the First Cuboid Conjecture, which states that for all positive coprime integers a, b with a ≠ b, a certain degree-8 polynomial P_{a,b}(t) over ℤ is irreducible. This conjecture was proposed by Shapirov in "Perfect cuboids and irreducible polynomials" (arXiv:1108.5348) as part of a family of three conjectures whose combined truth would imply the nonexistence of a perfect Euler brick. The proof first analyses rational factors and the symmetry F(−x) vs F(x) to reduce irreducibility of the degree-8 polynomial to irreducibility of a degree-4 factor Q_{a,b}, and the coprime branch to a Diophantine identity. Irreducibility of Q is in turn reduced to the quartic Diophantine equation x⁴ + 34x²y² + y⁴ = z², whose only trivial solutions are established by Fermat-style infinite descent. The formal proof was autonomously discovered by the AlphaProof Nexus agent; an independent informal proof using rank-zero elliptic curves was given by Asiryan (arXiv:2510.11768).
